title: Operator coordinator: CI/CD, image signing & adaptive rollout playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft playbook that captures an operator-centric CI/CD and release workflow for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It focuses on orchestration patterns (operator coordinator), artifact provenance (build -> scan -> sign), and adaptive rollout strategies that work in airgapped and VPC environments.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target clusters: customer-managed Kubernetes (1.22+), single-control-plane or multi-zone control planes.
- Packaging: Helm charts for application components + an operator (lightweight control-plane) that coordinates upgrades, preflight checks, and rollout waves.
- Artifact storage: OCI registry (external or mirrored into an airgap blob store), signed images and attestations (cosign), SBOMs attached.
- GitOps: ArgoCD as the canonical deployment mechanism in customer clusters. Argo app-of-apps pattern recommended.
- Terraform: used for infra bootstrap (VPC networking, cluster provisioning, registry mirrors, KMS bindings).
- Team responsibilities: eng-private-deployments owns operator code, release patterns, and recommended Terraform modules; platform-eng owns shared infra modules.

Quick flow summary (single paragraph):
CI builds image -> static scans and SBOM generation -> sign image and attestation -> publish to registry -> build Helm chart & bundle OCI chart (with signed image refs and SBOM links) -> push chart to chart-registry or OCI repo -> GitOps (PR to customer overlay repo updates chartRef/tag) -> ArgoCD detects change -> operator coordinator runs preflight -> progressive rollout per policy (canary/blue-green/traffic-shift) -> post-rollout validation + promote.

Operator coordinator pattern (high level):
- Role: lightweight controller installed in the customer cluster that performs preflight checks, triggers Argo app sync waves, tracks rollout signals, and can execute remediation hooks.
- Advantages: centralizes cluster-aware checks (node labels, taints, resource capacity), reduces need for manual runbooks, can orchestrate cross-chart upgrades.
- Design notes: controller should be pluggable (admit custom checks as CRD), expose a simple CRD like ReleasePlan with fields for chart refs, rollout strategy, health probes, and rollback actions.

Terraform modules notes (quick reference):
- module.registry-mirror: inputs: upstream_registry_url, mirror_bucket, signing_key_location, allowlist_namespaces; outputs: mirror_endpoint, mirror_credentials_secret_id.
- module/kms-binding: inputs: customer_kms_arn, rotation_schedule, operator_service_account; outputs: kms_key_id, iam_policy_attachment.
- module/cluster-bootstrap: includes argocd install option, operator install toggle, optional CNI config, and nodepool tags for rollout targeting.
- Best practices: keep module interfaces minimal, provide examples for airgap (OCI bundle export/import scripts), and include a terraform plan check wrapper that diffs planned changes against a safety policy file.

Helm chart and CRD upgrade strategy:
- Strict chart versioning: follow semver and avoid backwards-incompatible known-breaking changes in patch/minor releases.
- CRD changes: ship CRDs in a separate chart or a pre-install job with explicit migration steps; operator should detect CRD schema changes and gate the rollout until a migration job completes.
- Values schema: keep a compatibility map in CHANGES.md, and provide a Helm post-renderer script for value shims when upgrading across major versions.
- Chart testing: unit tests for templates (helm unittest), integration harness that deploys to a short-lived cluster and runs smoke tests.

GitOps / Argo patterns and sync behavior:
- App-of-apps: a root repo per customer that points at environment overlays (dev/stage/prod). The operator coordinator uses a dedicated overlay to inject ReleasePlan CRs.
- Sync waves: use Argo sync waves to ensure CRDs and namespace prerequisites apply before application charts. Define sensible hooks for pre-sync validation.
- Auto-prune: avoid enabling aggressive auto-prune in airgapped clusters without good observability; instead prefer controlled cleanup steps by the operator.
- Health checks: Argo health checks + operator-level business probes (eg, inference endpoint responds within expected latency and returns correct schema).

Image signing and attestation (practical):
- Tooling: cosign for signing images and creating predicate attestations. Store cosign keys in KMS/HSM where possible; for airgapped installs, provide offline signing key import guidance.
- Signing policy: require image:tag to be signed with a recognized key OR have a detached attestation in the registry. Images without signatures are rejected by an admission policy.
- SBOMs: generate SPDX or CycloneDX for each build; attach SBOM to the image OCI manifest or to the attestation.
- Verification: admission controller (or operator preflight) verifies signature and attestation, checks SBOM for banned packages, and optionally runs vulnerability delta checks.

Promotion pipeline (recommended):
1) CI build pipeline produces image + SBOM + artefact metadata (git sha, build time).
2) Automated static analysis (SCA), license check, basic integration tests.
3) Vulnerability scan; if score > threshold, block and open issue.
4) Sign image & attestation (cosign) using ephemeral key derived from KMS (or offline HSM flow for airgap).
5) Tag as releasable and push to internal registry/mirror; publish Helm chart bundle referencing signed image digest.
6) Create PR to customer overlay repo (or update release branch) that points new chart digest.
7) Operator coordinator runs preflight checks on merge and triggers Argo sync per environment policy.

Adaptive rollout policies (examples):
- Canary-by-node-label: roll out to nodes with label rollout=canary first (10% of pods), monitor latency and error budget for a defined window.
- Gradual-pod-increment: increase replica count of new revision by X% every Y minutes, requiring healthy probe pass each step.
- Blue-green with traffic-split: support environments with service mesh; operator can create weight changes via mesh API.
- Emergency fast-failover: if critical errors detected or a crashloop occurs > N pods, operator marks release failed and triggers rollback to recorded previous digest.

Preflight checks matrix (examples operator runs):
- Cluster capacity: cpu/memory headroom for new scheduling + ephemeral KV cache storage checks.
- Helm dry-run + kube-diff fused: detect resource deletions or disallowed changes.
- Image signature verification and SBOM sanity.
- NodeOS/kernel compatibility if using special runtimes (ie, MIG, custom GPU drivers).
- Port conflicts and LoadBalancer availability checks for onprem LB controllers.

Rollback and hotfix paths:
- Rollback policy: operator records previous chart digest and full values snapshot; rollback is a single command (CR update) that re-applies previous revision with a safety window.
- Hotfix releases: allow a fast-path branch that builds a hotfix image, signs it, and triggers a targeted release CR that only touches affected service.
- Manual intervention: include a quick list of kubectl/argocd commands for an SRE to force sync or roll back and links to logs (kubectl logs -l release=...).

Testing and validation guidance:
- Upgrade matrix testing: maintain a 2x2 matrix of from-version -> to-version tests for all supported major/minor pairs.
- Performance regression harness: run typical traffic against a staging cluster under representative load; capture p50/p95/p99 token latencies for generation endpoints.
- E2E acceptance: scripted end-to-end tests that cover auth, key rotation, operator hooks, and failure injection.

Observability and SLOs during rollout:
- Metrics to monitor: rollout_progress, failed_checks, request_latency_p95, token_cost_per_request, pod_restart_rate.
- Alerts: automatic abort on resource-unavailable or repeated health-check failures; notify on-call via Slack + runbook link.
- Traces: correlate rollout operations with traces for warm-start cold-starts and model warmup amplifications.

Airgap / offline specifics:
- Artifact bundle: provide scripts to export OCI images + Helm chart bundle as a tarball with a manifest that includes checksums and cosign signatures.
- Signing keys: provide a documented offline signing procedure (hash -> sign with on-prem HSM -> import attestation into registry).
- Mirror verification: after mirror import, run an operator preflight step that re-verifies signatures and SBOMs in the mirrored registry before enabling sync.

Security and compliance notes:
- Least-privilege: operator service account should have tightly scoped RBAC; terraform modules grant minimal IAM needed to bootstrap only.
- Audit trail: every release CR and operator decision should create an audit event stored externally (or sent to customer's audit endpoint), including cosign key id and build metadata.
- Key rotation: recommend rotating signing keys annually and provide a dual-sign strategy during rotation window (old + new key signatures accepted).

Runbook snippets (cheat-sheet for on-call):
- Abort a rollout: kubectl patch releaseplan <name> -p '{"spec":{"abort":true}}'
- Force rollback: kubectl apply -f rollback-previous-values.yaml OR argocd app rollback <app> <rev>
- Re-trigger preflight: kubectl annotate releaseplan/<name> operator.redwood/revalidate=true
- Inspect attestations: cosign verify --key $KMS_KEY_ID <image>@sha256:<digest>

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Offline signing UX: how to make an easy-to-follow CLI flow for enterprise security teams in airgapped mode (low effort, auditable)?
- Compatibility matrix with older ArgoCD versions customers might run (we need to support 2.5+ ideally).
- Should operator embed a limited admission webhook or rely on customer-managed admission controller? Tradeoffs: control vs responsibility.
- Define clear thresholds for vulnerability delta gating (CVSS-based? weighted by exploit maturity?).
- Terraform module examples: flesh out mirror import scripts and example pipelines for Azure/AWS/GCP airgap mirrors.

Next steps / action items:
- (Avery) draft a minimal ReleasePlan CRD spec and share prototype manifest.
- (Jun) prototype cosign offline signing helper and write documentation for airgap ops.
- (Sofia) create Terraform example repo for registry mirror + KMS binding.
- (Liam) build an integration test harness for operator coordinator that runs in CI and in a staged onprem lab.

Appendix: quick links and references:
- cosign docs: https://github.com/sigstore/cosign
- ArgoCD sync waves / hooks: https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/sync-waves/
author_notes: Draft style: intentionally conversational with TODOs and open questions. This lives in Drive as the working source for cross-team alignment on operator-centric release mechanics for private deployments. Expect follow-up PRs and a cleaned final playbook post-prototype testing.
